vm_revision_requirement.title: No file revised across assistant messages
vm_revision_requirement.description: Some counted file of the snapshot (the entrypoint, or the code it runs) must take its final content from at least the published min_file_writes (2 by default) assistant messages that write or edit it: each one writes the file (a Write, an Edit, a patch or a heredoc naming it) and is where one of the lines the file ends with first appears. Only a tool call writes a file: code an assistant message shows in its text, a fenced block included, writes none, and an edit counts where the call carries its old and new text (or a patch) for the file it names. A file written once in full and never revised counts 1, however often it was rewritten whole before.

eligibility.policy_status: Unresolved; house bot escalated to team, no sponsor/team answer observed

house_reply.body: entry_size caps the entry's tree at max_entry_bytes 8192, a symlink counting 0, and the deliverables require main.ts and a LICENSE with an OSI-approved license as files at the submitted commit; thinking_reproduces (min_authored 0.3, max_unwritten_share 0.4, entrypoints main.ts) requires the transcripts to show the agent writing the code, with the entrypoint carrying at least one authored line. Those provisions set what the snapshot and the transcripts must hold, but the published facts do not decide whether an interpreter's executable source may arrive through an entry environment secret instead of files in the snapshot, or how a secret-supplied implementation would count for the size tie break. I have passed this to the make.fun team. [comment link omitted]

eligibility.inference: For the tested 19-byte direct-eval entrypoint and 7-byte filename, inserting a second source line needs at least one extra byte, reaching at least 27. A valid separate retained line origin still requires genuine editing and verification. Matching the current 27-byte cutoff loses its earlier-receipt tie. This is a limitation of the tested architecture, not a proof that every possible implementation is impossible.
